previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, seizure disorder, diabetes, and bipolar disorder was admitted after experiencing a seizure triggered by severe right-sided abdominal pain that began while lifting bags. He also reported nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and fever. Imaging confirmed chronic calcific pancreatitis with no acute features and interval removal of a prior pancreatic stent. His white blood cell count was elevated, and he had a seizure during a CT scan. He was managed with pain control, pancreatic enzymes, and adjustment of his Dilantin dose due to subtherapeutic levels. His diet was advanced from clear liquids to a low-fat diet, and he remained seizure-free. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue medications, avoid heavy lifting, and follow up with GI and neurology.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for a flare of your pancreatitis causing 
nausea and vomitting. You were given medications for nausea and 
pain control. You were slowly advanced to a regular diet that 
you were able to tolerate at the time of discharge. Your 
seizures were evaluated by neurology and you were determined to 
not need any anti-seizure medications. Your pain was well 
controlled at the time of discharge. Some of your blood pressure 
medications were changed. You are to take your Clonidine once a 
day instead of twice a day for a week and stop taking the 
medication all together.
.
Take all medications as prescribed and go to all scheuduled 
follow up appointments.
.
Please contact your physician or return to the ED if you have 
worsening of your pancreatitis and abdominal pain with nausea 
and vomitting. Come to the ED if you have another seizure 
episode.
